Quote check: selection.md contains no verbatim paper quotes, so the check passes trivially. citations.json is unchanged ([]) because no paper is cited.

Spec line references: I re-read each spec_problem.md line I cite. L3-5 (dry run, not citable), L42 (t_99 = 0.4666), L46-47 (peak 1/8), L50-52 (dimensionless form), L98-100 (Dirichlet ends; end flux qL/2), L108-111 (out of scope), L109 (NumPy toy/heat1d.py), L129-130 (brief fixes FD + backward Euler). Each matches the text.

Hand-checked derivations: D1 (second difference exact on quadratics, from the Taylor remainder). D2 (nodal exactness of the steady state, using eigenvalues lambda_k = (4/h^2) sin^2(k pi h/2) > 0). D3 and D4 (backward Euler mode factor in (0,1); M-matrix bounds 0 <= theta <= theta_s). D7 (P1 Green's-function nodal exactness). D8 (consistent-mass M-matrix needs dtau >= h^2/6, i.e. 4.07e-5 for h = 1/64). D8b (lumped P1 is the same as FD-BE). D9 (series coefficients 4/(k pi)^3 for odd k; the check sum at xi = 1/2 equals 1/8).

Hand-computed numbers: lambda_1(h = 1/64) ≈ 9.8676. Slowest-mode backward Euler error at dtau = 1e-3 is about 2.34e-4 (0.19% of the 1/8 peak). Residual transient at tau = 1 is about 6.7e-6. Series tail for K = 11 is about 2.7e-4. DOFs: 63 (FD, P1), 64 (quadratic B-spline).

summary: I wrote derivation/selection.md with three candidates for the toy rod: finite differences with backward Euler (FD-BE), Galerkin finite elements, and the closed-form eigenfunction series. Each comes with derived failure modes, DOF counts for a reference case (N = 64, dtau = 1e-3), fit to the NumPy toy solver, and verification steps. A comparison table and a recommendation follow. I recommend FD-BE (branch feat/heat1d-fd-be): it is what the brief specifies, it stays stable and within 0 ≤ θ ≤ 1/8 for any time step, and it matches the parabola exactly at the nodes. The series serves as the reference for the transient convergence test, because the steady test cannot detect spatial order. No papers are cited and citations.json stays empty: the guard blocked library_search.py and scratch Python at this stage, so every claim rests on spec lines or hand derivations written out in the file.
